title: Watchtower ops outline — 2026-04-10 shift summary
content:
Brief summary

This note covers the 04/10 overnight watch (US-EAST -> EU handoff). Primary on-call was Marcus Velez, I covered the last 3 hours and am handing off to Priya Nair for the daytime window. The shift saw one medium-severity incident (regional kv-cache invalidation causing tail latency spikes on hosted-api v2) and a handful of smaller alerts (pod restarts during autoscaler churn, a flaky healthcheck on metrics-proxy).

Shift timeline (concise)
- 02:18 UTC — First alert: p95 latency for /v1/generate rose from 120ms -> 1.2s in us-east-1. Alert rule: hosted-api.p95.latency > 800ms for 3m. Pager triggered.
- 02:20 UTC — Marcus triaged, noted a coordinated increase in KV cache miss rate from 15% -> 94% on shards serving model-deployment v2.
- 02:28 UTC — Emergency mitigation: switched affected route to fallback model-variant v2-quant at the routing layer to restore steady latency. Pinged infra team channel.
- 02:35 UTC — Temporary autoscaling rule applied to increase dedicated pool capacity for v2 tasks (scaled +4 GPUs).
- 03:05 UTC — Latency normalized to baseline. Began detailed post-incident data collection.
- 04:05 UTC — Observed multiple metrics-proxy /healthz failing intermittently in us-east; restarted deployment, stabilized.
- 06:10 UTC — Pod churn detected in batch-worker-3 due to node reprovisioning. Evicted pods recovered on other nodes automatically.

Incident: Regional kv-cache invalidation (medium)
Summary: A coordination bug in the cache-invalidator service caused mass invalidation messages to be published to the us-east cache shards for model-deployment v2. This led to a very high cold-KV rate and resulted in p95 latency spikes for text generation endpoints. No customer data exposure. Approx incident window: 02:18–03:05 UTC.

Root cause (current hypothesis)
- A recent change in cache-invalidator (PR #811) added a multi-shard invalidation path but did not include a safety throttle for large keysets.
- During a roll of model-deployment v2, the rollout triggered a full-key reindex in the control plane; invalidator responded by enqueuing full-shard invalidations without batching.
- The serving runtime experienced a flood of KV misses, generating heavy reads to the backing parameter store and exhausting some per-shard IO limits, causing increased token generation latency.

Immediate mitigations taken
- Fallback routing to quantized variant v2-quant for the affected customer region (02:28 UTC). This bypassed the hot-path using the heavy KV lookups.
- Temporarily increased capacity for dedicated serving pool for v2 (02:35 UTC).
- Scoped the invalidation queue processors to limit concurrent invalidations (workaround patch rolled: reverted bad behavior at 03:02 UTC).
- Added monitoring alert for invalidation enqueue rate > 5000/min per-shard.

Evidence collected
- Logs: invalidator service traces show 1.2M invalidation messages pushed in 2 minutes (link: github logs archived, see linked_artifacts).
- Metrics: KV hit rate drop graph saved to /metrics/snapshots/2026-04-10/us-east-kv-drop.png (uploaded to SRE drive).
- Traces: APM traces show increased downstream datastore latency correlated with our token generation calls.

Runbook gaps identified
- No explicit throttle defined for full-shard invalidations (runbook section missing guidance).
- Rollback steps for invalidator are not clearly documented; current playbook assumes safe idempotent invalidations.
- No synthetic test to simulate high invalidation churn against live shards.

Follow-ups and owners (short list)
- Marcus Velez: follow up with serving-runtime team to add backpressure in invalidator (JIRA: SRE-4123).
- Sofia Martinez: update kv-cache runbook draft with explicit throttle and emergency rollback steps (Confluence draft referenced).
- Liam Chen (me): add a synthetic canary job to simulate invalidation bursts against a staging shard and add to CI gating for future PRs. (linked PR: serving-runtime#811 review notes).
- Infra On-call (owner: TBD): evaluate IO limits on us-east shard hosts and propose quota changes if needed.

Action items (actionable, short)
- [SRE-4123] Patch invalidator to add batch-windowing (owner: Marcus) — target: 2026-04-13
- Update runbook: add step-by-step rollback and a safe-mode flag for invalidator (owner: Sofia) — target: 2026-04-12
- Create canary job and CI test for invalidation churn (owner: Liam) — target: 2026-04-16
- Post-incident blameless review meeting scheduled: 2026-04-12 15:00 PDT (calendar invite sent to eng-sre + serving-runtime + infra)

Smaller alerts and notes
- metrics-proxy flaky healthcheck (04:05 UTC): root cause appears to be CPU steal on underlying node; restarted pod and marked node for maintenance. Follow-up: infra to cordon node and investigate noisy-neighbor (owner: infra-sre).
- batch-worker-3 pod churn (06:10 UTC): caused by scheduled node reprovisioning overlapping with a warmup window; scheduling policy to be adjusted to avoid reprovisions within 30 minutes of scheduled batch window. Owner: platform-engineering.

Commands and debug snippets used (for handover)
- kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=hosted-api-v2 -o wide
- curl -sS 'https://internal-metrics/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_miss_rate{region=\"us-east\",model=\"v2\"}'
- dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/testfile bs=1M count=100 && ls -lh /tmp/testfile (used in node IO test during triage)

Notes to next shift (Priya)
- Watch kv invalidation enqueue rate for first 2 hours after your start; threshold alert added but verify good signal (rule: invalidator.enqueue_rate_per_shard > 1000/min).
- Double-check rollout status for any ongoing v2 rollouts; there is a rollout in progress that was paused at canary stage—do not resume without coordination. Link to rollout: internal control-plane UI (see confluence link).
- If p95 increases and kv-miss spikes again, prefer routing to v2-quant + scaled capacity rather than immediate rollback; rollback of model version has customer-visible risk.

Unresolved questions
- Did the invalidator change get merged to other regions without the same canary gating? Need verification. (Owner: Marcus)
- What is the long-term plan for shard IO quotas as more models are pinned to the same shards? (Owner: infra lead)

Post-incident retrospective notes (brief)
- What went well: Fast detection via p95 alerts, quick fallback to quantized variant restored SLA quickly, good cross-team comms in infra and runtime channels.
- Improvements: Add backpressure and throttle to invalidator, improve runbook rollback clarity, introduce canary tests for invalidation churn.

Attachments and references
- JIRA: SRE-4123 (invalidator backpressure)
- GitHub PR: serving-runtime#811 (change that introduced multi-shard invalidation)
- Confluence: kv-cache-invalidation-runbook-draft (please add edits inline)

Handoff acceptance checklist (next on-call)
- [ ] Confirm alerts are green for hosted-api.p95.latency and invalidator.enqueue_rate
- [ ] Review paused rollouts and confirm no auto-resume scheduled
- [ ] Acknowledge calendar invite for post-incident review

If anything is urgent during your watch, call me (Liam) on mobile or ping @liam.chen in #sre-ops.

End of note.
